ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle centered at F, and a horizontal line segment passes through H, F, L; the part from H to F is labeled 8 beside it. Point K is at the upper right of the circle, and an oblique line segment FK is drawn from F to K; from K downward to L there is a vertical line segment LK, and there is a right angle mark at L, indicating that FL and LK are perpendicular. Reasoning: The problem gives FH ≅ FL, so FL = FH = 8. It also gives FK = 17. In right triangle FLK, FK is the hypotenuse, and FL and LK are the two legs. By the Pythagorean theorem, LK = sqrt(FK^2 - FL^2) = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = sqrt(225) = 15.

raw_record.question_text:
In $\odot F, \overline{F H} \cong \overline{F L}$ and $\mathrm{FK}=17$.
Find $LK$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: the segment HF is labeled 8, F is the circle center, FK is drawn to point K on the circle, and the vertical segment through K meets the horizontal segment at L with a right-angle mark at L. From the text, FH ≅ FL, so FL = FH = 8. Also the text gives FK = 17. Then use right triangle FLK, where FK is the hypotenuse and FL is one leg. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: LK = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = sqrt(225) = 15.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at F with a vertical chord through K and M, and with FL drawn perpendicular to that chord at L. The image labels FH = 8, and the text says FH ≅ FL, so the perpendicular distance from the center F to the chord KM is FL = 8. Since FK is a radius and the text gives FK = 17, use the circle/chord distance relation: for a chord at distance d from the center in a circle of radius r, the half-chord length is sqrt(r^2 - d^2). The segment LK is the upper half of chord KM, so LK = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = 15.
